pages.text: "I will do it!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, draped his green scarf around his neck. Cold wind whistled round the alley corner.
"Today I will wrap it myself!" He clenched both hands. Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, watched.
But the scarf slipped loose. After one turn, the end hung down and dragged in the snow. "Oh, loose again!"
His neck felt chilly and bare. Nono lowered his head. "I cannot even tie a scarf..." His beak trembled.
Grandpa sat by the door and stretched out the scarf. "This long bit goes once around your neck." Nono tilted his head.
Grandpa opened a round gap in the scarf with a finger. "Wrap around, tuck it in!" "That is all?" Nono gulped.
First, around the neck! Nono wrapped it once. "Around!" His neck no longer felt bare.
Second, tuck it in! He pushed the long end through the gap. The knot held. Kiki clapped.
The wind blew, but the knot stayed tied. "One, around your neck! Two, through the gap! Three, a gentle tug!" Nono raised both hands.
Next morning, Nono tied the scarf himself. Kiki lifted him in a hug. Learn one step at a time, and you can do it yourself. He touched his green scarf and beamed. "Wrap around, tuck it in!"
